title: Path to Prior-Data Fitted Relational Models via Learned Latent Multi-table Representations
abstract: arXiv:2610.23073v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Prior-data fitted networks (PFNs) show that pretraining on large populations of synthetic tasks can enable generalization to unseen datasets with little or no downstream fine-tuning. This paradigm is effective for transformer-based tabular and relational foundation models such as RDB-PFN, but remains largely unexplored for graph-based relational models built on message passing. We pretrain the graph-based relational foundation model Griffin on large collections of synthetic relational databases and ask whether curriculum learning, which benefits transformer-based relational learners, also improves message-passing representations. Rather than fine-tune on downstream tasks, we use the pretrained encoder as a general-purpose relational representation learner and pass its latent representations to a frozen in-context predictor (\ticl{}); no component is trained on the target task. On 16 real-world relational classification tasks, evaluated

translated_title: 基于学习的潜在多表表示通往先验数据拟合关系模型的路径
translated_abstract: 先验数据拟合网络（PFNs）表明，在大量合成任务上进行预训练能够使模型泛化到未见过的数据集，而几乎无需或完全无需下游微调。这一范式在基于Transformer的表格和关系基础模型（如RDB-PFN）上已被证明有效，但对于基于消息传递构建的图基关系模型而言，该范式在很大程度上仍待探索。我们在大规模合成关系数据库集合上预训练图基关系基础模型Griffin，并探究对基于Transformer的关系学习者有益的课程学习，是否同样能改进消息传递表示。我们没有在下游任务上进行微调，而是将预训练编码器作为通用的关系表示学习器，并将其潜在表示传递给一个冻结的上下文内预测器（TabICL）；没有任何组件在目标任务上接受训练。在16个真实世界的关系分类任务上进行了评估……
tldr: 该论文首次将先验数据拟合（PFN）范式拓展到基于消息传递的图关系模型，通过在合成关系数据库上预训练Griffin编码器，并将其潜在表示输入冻结的上下文内预测器，在目标任务零训练的情况下实现了对真实世界关系分类任务的泛化，并验证了课程学习对消息传递表示的增益。
en_tdlr: This work extends the prior-data fitted network (PFN) paradigm to message-passing-based graph relational models by pretraining the Griffin encoder on synthetic relational databases and feeding its latent multi-table representations into a frozen in-context predictor, achieving generalization on real-world relational classification with zero target-task training and showing that curriculum learning also benefits message-passing representations.
